sentences.quote: Philipp Navratil (born 1976) is an Austrian-Swiss business executive and has been the chief executive of Nestle since September 2025.
sentences.text: Philipp Navratil, born in 1976 in Zurich, is an Austrian-Swiss executive who has been chief executive of Nestle since September 2025.

sentences.quote: On leaving university in 2001, Navratil joined Nestle as an internal auditor and went on to hold various commercial roles in Central America for the company.
sentences.text: He holds an MBA from the University of St. Gallen, joined Nestle in 2001 as an international auditor, held commercial positions in Central America and was appointed country manager for Nestle Honduras in 2009.

From 2013 he led the coffee and beverage business in Mexico, and in 2020 became senior vice president and head of the Coffee Strategic Business Unit, shaping global strategy for the Nescafe and Starbucks brands.

sentences.quote: In July 2024 he became CEO of Nespresso, a capital-intensive "system business"
sentences.text: In July 2024 he became CEO of Nespresso S.A., joining the Nestle Executive Board on January 1, 2025.
The board appointed him CEO following the dismissal of Laurent Freixe, and weeks into the role he announced a cost-cutting plan cutting 16,000 jobs, targeting savings by the end of 2027.

sentences.text: Pablo Isla succeeded Paul Bulcke as chair effective October 1, 2025, alongside CEO Philipp Navratil, appointed in September 2025 after Laurent Freixe's dismissal.

In September 2026 the board named Manuela Bernasconi, General Counsel for Zone Americas, as Group General Counsel and Group Executive Board member effective January 1, 2027, with Leanne Geale retiring after seven years.
Antonia Wanner became Chief Communications and Sustainability Officer and executive board member on September 1, 2026, after Lisa Gibby decided to return to the United States.
Fatima Francisco and Thomas Jordan were nominated to the board for election at the April 16, 2026 AGM.

sentences.quote: CEO Philipp Navratil held the full-year guidance of 3% to 4% organic growth and pressed ahead with a CHF 3 billion cost-savings target and 16,000 job cuts.
sentences.text: Navratil became CEO in September 2025 after the abrupt departure of Laurent Freixe, and set RIG-led growth as the top priority alongside headcount reductions of 16,000 over two years and higher savings targets, with a CHF 3 billion cost-savings goal.

First-half 2026 showed organic growth of 3.6% with real internal growth improving to 1.5% and savings running slightly ahead of plan, though net profit fell 31% to CHF 3.47 billion on a CHF 1.3 billion write-down tied to businesses being sold and restructuring costs.

Capital allocation has turned to portfolio pruning: a 50:50 waters and premium beverages joint venture expected to yield about CHF 2.8 billion net proceeds, vitamins and ice cream classified as held for sale, the yfood stake bought and Blue Bottle divested.

sentences.text: Nestle's RIG-led growth strategy is showing traction, with H1-2026 organic growth of 3.6% and real internal growth improving from 1.2% in Q1 to 1.8% in Q2.

sentences.quote: Coffee was Nestle's strongest major category in the first half, delivering organic growth of 7.5%, including 4.7% pricing and 2.9% RIG.
sentences.text: Coffee is the main engine, delivering 7.5% organic growth in the first half, alongside emerging markets at 7.1% organic growth excluding China.
Management is expanding growth platforms to 30% of sales with CHF 0.6 billion of additional investment in 2026, funded by CHF 3.0 billion of Fuel for Growth savings targeted by end-2027.

sentences.quote: Portfolio reshaping includes exiting ice cream and a partial withdrawal from bottled water, with divestments weighing on near-term reported sales.
sentences.text: Portfolio reshaping continues, including exiting ice cream and a partial withdrawal from bottled water.
Guidance supports cash returns, with organic growth of 3-4% and free cash flow above CHF 9 billion for 2026.
